processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Cast ingot homogenized at 1100 °C for 2 hr prior to hot forging.
Hot forged to 50% thickness reduction in the temperature range 1050-800 °C followed by air cooling to room temperature.

Hot forged samples hot rolled (soaking 1100 °C, 2hr) in the range 1050-800 °C in two passes (reheating 1100 °C, 5 min between passes), 50% thickness reduction each pass, finally water quenched to RT from finish rolling temperature (~800 °C).
processing_steps.reduction_ratio: 50% thickness reduction in each pass (two passes)

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Surface machining up to 1 mm depth on both sides of hot rolled sheet to remove the surface oxide layer, leaving a 3 mm thick sheet.
processing_steps.reduction_ratio: 1 mm depth on both sides (final sheet thickness 3 mm)

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: HRQ 3 mm sheet intercritically annealed at 750 °C (IA750) for 120 min, followed by air cooling to room temperature; this is the defining step for the IA750_120 Min specimen.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: at least three samples tested; average values reported
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: subsize tensile specimens machined by wire EDM along the rolling direction

phases_present.morphology: highly stable, formed during solidification; structure/morphology remains unchanged after intercritical annealing; Al-enriched
matrix phase that increases with annealing as reverted austenite dissolves into it
blocky/coarse retained austenite; Mn and C enriched
phases_present.volume_fraction: ~30% (retained austenite, untransformed + reverted, before tensile test); ~28% after tensile test

phases_present.morphology: few needle and globular types (SEM Fig. 4D2); progressively dissolving into intercritical ferrite with increasing annealing time

structures.overall_structure: Intercritically annealed (750 °C, 120 min then air cooled) specimen showing few needle and globular types of reverted austenite, which are largely dissolved into intercritical ferrite (α), resulting in a microstructure of mostly intercritical ferrite (α) and untransformed austenite together with highly stable δ-ferrite; martensite present in the HRQ precursor has been largely transformed/dissolved.
